comment: The canonical persona questions the analytics MCP surface answers deterministically. The exact question string here is THE question — no test may refer to an older draft. Every entry has an executable case in analyticsmcpquestions_integration_test.go, held in both directions by TestEveryCanonicalQuestionHasExecutableProof.

questions.question: How much pipeline do I have right now?
questions.expects: An omitted scope resolves to the rep's own deals, never the workspace.

questions.question: Show me the whole company's pipeline by owner.
questions.expects: Refused outright — never quietly narrowed to a population the answer does not name.

questions.question: Add our EUR, USD, and VND pipeline and give me one number.
questions.expects: Per-deal conversion to the base currency; a deal with no applicable rate is excluded from the money and still counted, never guessed at rate 1.

questions.question: How much open pipeline does my team have in each stage right now?
questions.expects: One row per stage, open deals only, the caller's own population — a colleague's deals and closed deals both stay out.

questions.question: Which stages are taking longer than normal for my team?
questions.expects: Days in the current stage, read through the stage-age entity under the caller's own lens. Fewer than five deals are withheld whole, so one deal's age never wears a statistic's name.

questions.question: Is our pipeline too concentrated in a few large deals?
questions.expects: Count and value together, plus the largest deal — concentration is the gap between them, and a count alone cannot show it.

questions.question: Which open deals are stuck and have no agreed next step?
questions.expects: The shared stalled rule over the report path. `stalled` is a report FILTER and the analytics schema publishes dimensions and measures only, so an agent asking this through run_analytics_query is told the field does not exist.

questions.question: What is my team's win rate by deal count and by value this quarter?
questions.expects: Count and value are separate readings: six wins at 10k beside five losses at 60k is a majority of deals won and a majority of the money lost, and one number cannot say both.

questions.question: Which lead sources created the most won revenue?
questions.expects: Won revenue by the source the deal carries, in base currency. The lost cohort is the discriminator: win-loss already excludes open deals, so an engine ignoring the status filter would count losses as revenue.

questions.question: Why are we losing, and how many deals support each recorded reason?
questions.expects: One row per reason somebody WROTE on the deal, counted. The won cohort is the discriminator: a won deal carries no reason, so an engine that skipped the status filter reports a bucket of wins under no reason at all and reads as the commonest cause of loss.

questions.question: How much of my team's pipeline is commit, best case and pipeline right now?
questions.expects: One row per forecast category, in base currency. A commit deal past its close date reads as slipped, never as commit, and a colleague outside the team stays out.

questions.question: How much of my team's open pipeline is due to close in each month?
questions.expects: One row per expected-close month over open deals only. A deal with no close date has its own row, and a closed or off-team deal stays out.

questions.question: Which of my team's committed deals have slipped?
questions.expects: A commit or best-case deal with a past or missing close date counts. A pipeline-category deal with a past date does not, and neither does an off-team deal.

questions.question: Who on my team owns the most open pipeline?
questions.expects: One row per teammate, ranked by open pipeline value. An owner outside the team is never named.

questions.question: Which reps on my team won the most this quarter?
questions.expects: Wins closed this quarter only. A loss, a win from last quarter and a win by an off-team rep stay out.

questions.question: What did I win and lose this month?
questions.expects: Only the rep's own closed deals in the month. win-loss covers the company by default, so a colleague's deals and the rep's own older wins both have to stay out.

questions.question: How much did we win this quarter compared with last quarter?
questions.expects: Won money in base currency per quarter. A lost deal never counts as won money.

questions.question: Which customers have the most open deals?
questions.expects: One row per company over open deals only. A company whose deals are all closed is not listed.

questions.question: How many leads do we have in each status, including the ones we promoted or disqualified?
questions.expects: The promoted and disqualified statuses are counted although those leads are archived.
